\begin{definition}[Sign-encoded Boolean functions of bounded degree]
\lean{FABL.f₂PolynomialSignClass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p161-b002}
For natural numbers $n$ and $d$, let $\mathcal{C}_{n,d}$ be the set of functions
$F:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ for which there is a Boolean function $f$ on
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of algebraic degree at most $d$ such that $F$ is the real sign encoding
of $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Translation invariance of a polynomial sign class]
\lean{FABL.isTranslationClosed_f₂PolynomialSignClass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTranslationClosed, FABL.domainTranslate, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_domainTranslate, FABL.f₂PolynomialSignClass}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural numbers $n$ and $d$, the class of real-valued functions on the
$n$-dimensional cube over $\bbf_2$ obtained by encoding $\bbf_2$-valued functions of
algebraic degree at most $d$ as signs is closed under translations: if $F$ belongs to
this class and $z$ is any cube point, then $x\mapsto F(x+z)$ also belongs to it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of density expectation]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation_mono}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation_mono}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.nonneg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb
F_2^n$, and let $F,G:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $F(x)\le G(x)$ for every $x$.
Then the expectation of $F$ under $\varphi$ is at most the expectation of $G$ under
$\varphi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Adding a constant to a density expectation]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation_add_const}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation_add_const}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb
F_2^n$, let $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $c\in\mathbb R$. The expectation of
$F+c$ under $\varphi$ equals the expectation of $F$ under $\varphi$ plus $c$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\psi$ and $\phi$ be probability densities on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
(nonnegative functions with uniform expectation one), and let
$F:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The expectation of $F$ with respect to the convolution
of $\psi$ and $\phi$ equals the expectation of the convolution of $\phi$ with $F$ with
respect to $\psi$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
For every integer $n \ge 0$, let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be probability densities on the
Boolean cube $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let $F:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$. Then
\[
\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\psi}\!\left[(\phi*F)(z)^2\right]
=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\phi}\,\mathbb{E}_{y'\sim\phi}\,\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\psi}\!\left[F(z+y)F(z+y')\right],
\]
where each expectation is weighted by the indicated density and addition is
coordinatewise modulo $2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product identity for translated sign encodings]
\lean{FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_add_translates}
\label{FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_add_translates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signEncode_add, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be a Boolean function, and let $x,y,y'\in\mathbb
F_2^n$. Encode a bit $b$ as the real sign $(-1)^b$. Then the product of the real sign
encodings of $f(x+y)$ and $f(x+y')$ equals the real sign encoding, evaluated at $x$, of
the function $z\mapsto f(z+y)+f(z+y')$, with addition in $\mathbb F_2^n$ and $\mathbb
F_2$, respectively.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Convolution with the uniform density]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolution_eq_uniform_of_right}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolution_eq_uniform_of_right}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolution, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.convolution, FABL.convolution_apply}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\psi$ and $\phi$ be probability densities on $\mathbb F_2^n$. If $\phi$ is
identically $1$, then the convolution of $\psi$ with $\phi$ is identically $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive convolution powers of the uniform density]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolutionPower_eq_uniform_of_pos}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolutionPower_eq_uniform_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolution, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolutionPower, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolution_eq_uniform_of_right}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb F_2^n$ that is identically $1$, and let
$d$ be a positive integer. The $d$-fold convolution power of $\phi$ is also identically
$1$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.violaError_zero}

zero when $\varepsilon=0$.

\difficulty{7}
Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb F_2^n$ whose nonzero Fourier
coefficients all have absolute value at most $\varepsilon$, where $0<\varepsilon\leq1$.
If $d\geq1$, then the $d$-fold convolution power of $\phi$ approximates the uniform
expectation of every real sign encoding of an $\mathbb F_2$-valued function on $\mathbb
F_2^n$ of algebraic degree at most $d$: the absolute difference between its expectation
under that density and its uniform expectation is at most $9\varepsilon^{1/2^{d-1}}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that is $\varepsilon$-biased,
where $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$. For every integer $d\geq1$, the $d$-fold convolution
power of $\phi$ fools every sign-valued function represented by a polynomial over
$\mathbb{F}_2$ of algebraic degree at most $d$, with error at most
$9\varepsilon^{1/2^{d-1}}$.
\end{theorem}
